title: Stored and displayed totals match exactly in multi-currency transaction
gherkin:
Feature: Multi-currency conversion integrity
  Scenario: Verify stored total matches displayed total in multi-currency transaction
    Given a transaction with amount 100.00 USD
    And the customer's display currency is EUR
    And the conversion rate is 0.92 EUR per USD
    When the transaction is stored in the financial system
    And the customer views the transaction in their display currency
    Then the stored amount in USD is 100.00
    And the displayed amount in EUR is 92.00
    And the conversion calculation is 100.00 * 0.92 = 92.00
    And no rounding discrepancies exist between stored and displayed values
rationale: This test validates the core requirement that user-facing totals must always match persisted billing amounts exactly. It ensures that currency conversion does not introduce hidden discrepancies between what is stored in the financial system and what the customer sees.
usedContextItems: Multi-currency conversion must maintain integrity between stored financial records and customer-facing display totals|User-facing totals must always match persisted billing amounts exactly

title: Presentation simplification does not create audit discrepancies
gherkin:
Feature: Multi-currency conversion integrity
  Scenario: Prevent display-friendly simplification from creating audit mismatches
    Given a transaction with precise amount 100.456 USD
    And the customer's display currency is EUR
    And the conversion rate is 0.92 EUR per USD
    When the transaction is stored with full precision as 92.41952 EUR
    And the customer-facing display rounds to 92.42 EUR
    Then the audit trail records the precise stored value 92.41952 EUR
    And the displayed value 92.42 EUR is marked as a presentation format only
    And the billing system uses the precise stored value 92.41952 EUR, not the rounded 92.42 EUR
    And no financial discrepancy occurs between audit records and billing calculations
rationale: This test addresses the conflict between display-friendly simplification and precise value preservation. It ensures that while customer-facing displays may show rounded values for readability, the underlying stored values remain precise and are used for all billing and audit purposes, preventing silent overrides of pricing logic.

title: International billing does not override core pricing logic
gherkin:
Feature: Multi-currency conversion integrity
  Scenario: Prevent international billing from overriding pricing logic
    Given a product with base price 100.00 USD
    And a discount of 10% applies to the base price
    And the customer's billing currency is INR
    And the conversion rate is 82.50 INR per USD
    When the transaction is processed with international billing in INR
    Then the discount is applied to the base price first: 100.00 * 0.90 = 90.00 USD
    And the discounted amount is then converted: 90.00 * 82.50 = 7425.00 INR
    And the pricing logic is not overridden by international billing
    And the stored amount is 7425.00 INR
    And the displayed amount is 7425.00 INR
    And no alternative calculation (e.g., 100 * 82.50 * 0.90) produces a different result
rationale: This test ensures that international billing and currency conversion do not bypass or override core pricing logic. It validates that discounts and other pricing rules are applied before currency conversion, maintaining the integrity of the pricing system.
